current_episode.title: Power Responsive: flexibility is our hidden power

guest.titre: Head of Balancing Services Development and Delivery
guest.bio_context: Jonathan Wisdom oversees the development and delivery of balancing services at NISO, the National Energy System Operator. He is responsible for how parties participate in NISO's markets. His work focuses on demand-side flexibility and consumer engagement across the energy system.

context.transcript_excerpt: This conversation is brought to you by Modula, the payments automation platform. Hello, I'm Lily Gooden. Welcome to the Future of Utilities podcast. We are now joined by somebody very special. We're going to talk about NISO's power responsive program and how flexibility could be our superpower. We have a great guest, Jonathan Wisdom from NISO. Great to have you with us. First of all, tell us who you are and what you do. Thanks, Lily. Really pleased to be here with you all today. My name is Jonathan Wisdom, or John, so really happy for that as well. Perfect. This afternoon as we keep chatting. I look after the development and delivery of our balancing services at NISO, which is how parties participate in our markets. NISO is the national energy system operator. We're the company that today we keep the lights on, we operate the electricity system, but we also plan tomorrow's energy system. That means that everything wants to work holistically and we want to keep our hands around that holistically to make that work. Flexibility is a really important part of that. We want to make sure that consumers have the opportunity to participate across our energy system and be really involved. We're looking forward to this conversation. Brilliant. Let's start with flexibility because it is the word of the moment, really. Energy security starts at home in many ways. Flexibility is very important. If you just describe the Power Responsive program, what's it about? What's the mission and why? Absolutely. Power Responsive has been within NISO for a while. It probably came to fruition, to life around about 10 or 11 years ago. It's very much about engaging the market and understanding what demand-side participation could look like. NISO knows that it has a role as this whole system entity to drive flexibility and encourage its participation as much as possible in all of our products. What that means in practice for Power Responsive is that we worked with Ofgem and the government last year to really focus on how Power Responsive can evolve and change to drive forward these actions that we need to take. Power Responsive now has evolved into an entity that is now engaging directly with consumers, helping them bring their flexibility to market and being able to participate in the energy system like never before. What's the purpose? The purpose that we're hearing a lot of today is to be able to stabilize our demand for energy. I suppose that's very much part of it, is to be able to work, yes, with consumers, but also with suppliers to make sure that that two-way flow of energy is healthier, particularly in times where a lot of energy is needed. Absolutely. NISO, as the system operator, has a need to access these resources to enable us to operate that system and, as you say, keep that supply and demand in balance all the time. That's where flexibility can be really helpful and useful. We're no longer in a world where we have large centralized loads providing all of our generation. We're in a world where decentralized loads need to come and participate in our energy system like they haven't done before. Power Responsive is there to help consumers do that, to help consumers understand how to engage with suppliers and aggregators, to understand the capacity and the capability of what they have to offer us flexibility. Yes. Somebody looking at this from the outside and looking at the website and understanding what Power Responsive is in headline value only might think, okay, it's the big energy suppliers and it's not really involving me. Maybe you're a smaller partner, but who do you want to bring to the table? Who do you want this conversation to be with? Who needs to speak and who do we need to listen to? It's a great question. Across the energy system, we're moving to a world where consumers are not just taking energy from the network. They're able to change their behavior. The way the system has changed recently and certainly the introduction of new rul

pending_qa.q: Who does Power Responsive want to bring into the conversation and involve?
pending_qa.r: Power Responsive wants to work closely with domestic users through suppliers and aggregators, but particularly with industrial and commercial actors who want to understand their energy use better and how their loads can offer flexibility. The program aims to help consumers of all types—from cold storage and supermarkets to EV fleets—understand the value their flexibility can represent to their organizations.

pending_qa.q: What are the specific targets and goals for Power Responsive by 2030?
pending_qa.r: NISO published targets at the end of last year showing they currently have around 200 megawatts plus of participation. They want to grow that to around 950 megawatts, or even a gigawatt of flexibility participating in the market by 2030. That's the goal for how seriously they take the development of flexibility markets.

pending_qa.q: How does flexibility help balance the modern energy system?
pending_qa.r: The energy system has moved away from large centralized loads providing all generation to a world where decentralized loads need to participate in the energy system like never before. Flexibility is helpful and useful for NISO as the system operator because it allows access to resources needed to operate the system and keep supply and demand in balance all the time.

pending_qa.q: What barriers exist for consumers and businesses to participate in flexibility markets?
pending_qa.r: There is significant complexity in the market and industry that makes participation daunting from the outside. NISO is trying to take some of that complexity and challenge away to make engaging in the market more possible. The goal is to make participation and providing flexibility as easy as possible in a way that takes account of the business that consumers have to run.

pending_qa.q: What is NISO's commitment to the development of flexibility markets?
pending_qa.r: This is a core part of NISO's mission, role, purpose and vision to deliver growth in flexibility and growth in these markets. It is not something temporary but something they believe in and want to see developed and pushed forward. NISO has the Power Responsive function plus two other programs within NISO that are focused on enabling demand-side flexibility.
